source.title: Impartial Reporter and Farmers' Journal, 24 April 1924, p. 8 ("Fermanagh Nominations: New Co. Council — A Representative List")
source.publisher: Impartial Reporter and Farmers' Journal (via the Newspapers.com)

note: First election under the 1923 county electoral divisions. Nomination day was Tuesday 22 April 1924, and the Impartial Reporter of 24 April 1924, p. 8 ('Fermanagh Nominations: New Co. Council — A Representative List') prints the complete list division by division: 'As was anticipated neither the Sinn Fein nor Nationalist parties put forward any candidates, and the Unionists were returned unopposed.' The Ministry of Home Affairs order of 15 May 1924 (Belfast Gazette, 16 May 1924, No. 151, p. 793) then fixed 28 May 1924 as the day of election for the twenty county electoral divisions and reconstituted the council on 29 May. Nineteen divisions are recorded here; the twentieth, Belleek, drew no nomination in time and is omitted — the paper adding that Mr Erne Elliott, J.P., was expected to be co-opted for the seat. The same nomination day for the rural district councils is reported in the Belfast News-Letter of 24 April 1924, p. 5, which supplies the rural returns. Division names follow the 1927 return so the rounds join; the paper prints Larah for Laragh. The first meeting of the new council is reported in the Fermanagh Herald, 14 June 1924, p. 8. That the April list did produce the sitting council is borne out by the 1927 return, where Crozier (Ballinamallard), Brooke (Brookeborough), Barton (Clonelly), Cathcart (Monea), Thomas A. Graham (Lisnaskea), Stewart (Maguiresbridge) and J. W. H. Johnston (Newtownbutler) stand again for the same divisions. Returned unopposed.
